heading-home-body: Feel at Home in Your Body
paragraph-home-body-1: Imagine feeling so at home in your body that intimacy no longer feels like something you have to get right. Instead of doubting whether you're attractive enough, experienced enough, or getting it right, you begin to notice what you are feeling. You recognize your desires more clearly. You communicate them with confidence. You trust your boundaries. You become more curious, playful, and present—with yourself and with the people you choose to share intimacy.
paragraph-home-body-2: For many of us, this doesn't come naturally. We grow up surrounded by messages about what our bodies should look like, how relationships should unfold, and what 'good sex' is supposed to be. Dating apps, porn, social media, cultural expectations, and shame often teach us to compare ourselves, perform for others, or disconnect from our own experience.
paragraph-home-body-3: My work as a Somatic Intimacy Coach offers another possibility. This isn't about becoming a different person. It's about becoming more yourself. Over time, many clients discover that intimacy can feel clearer and more intuitive. Less performative and more alive. Less about meeting expectations and more about genuine connection—with themselves, their partners, and their bodies.
paragraph-home-body-4: I believe the quality of your intimacy is shaped by the quality of your attention.
paragraph-coaching-1: Somatic Intimacy Coaching combines conversation with embodied learning. Depending on your intentions, sessions may include dialogue, body-awareness practices, movement, breathwork, experiential exercises, and optional bodywork. Every session is tailored to your goals, and we move entirely at your pace.
paragraph-coaching-2: Unlike approaches that focus primarily on talking, this work invites you to notice what is happening in your body as it happens. Together we slow down, explore sensations, experiment with new choices, and practise skills that can transform how you experience intimacy beyond our sessions.
paragraph-coaching-3: Whether you're hoping to communicate more openly, feel more comfortable receiving pleasure, reconnect with your body after change, or simply discover what's possible, our work begins with curiosity rather than assumptions.
paragraph-coaching-4: I help people develop the skills most of us were never taught: listening to the body's signals, understanding desire, communicating boundaries, receiving touch, expanding pleasure, and making choices that feel authentic rather than automatic.
paragraph-coaching-5: If you're wondering whether this approach is right for you, I invite you to book a complimentary 20-minute introductory call with me. It's an opportunity to ask me questions, talk about what you're hoping to explore, and decide whether working together feels right.
paragraph-offerings-1: Everyone finds their own way into intimacy. Some people arrive with a specific question. Others simply know they want to feel more connected to themselves or to the people they love. Below are a few examples of where our work together might begin—not a checklist, but invitations into new possibilities.

expressing.heading: Expressing Desire with Confidence
expressing.text: Imagine being with a lover and instead of hoping they can read your mind, being able to say, “Slower,” “More pressure,” “I want you closer,” or “I’d prefer something else tonight.” Together we can explore how to recognize your desires, communicate your needs, and express boundaries with clarity and confidence, so that intimacy feels collaborative rather than uncertain.

presence.heading: From Performance to Presence
presence.text: During sex, many people wonder, “Am I doing this right?”, “Do I look good?”, “Is my partner enjoying themselves?” When attention shifts toward performance, it becomes difficult to notice your own experience. Through breath, movement, and somatic awareness, you can learn to return to what is happening inside your body—warmth, tension, excitement, hesitation, pleasure—so that intimacy becomes something you experience rather than perform.

boundaries.heading: Listening to Your Boundaries
boundaries.text: Sometimes we agree to something before realizing it doesn't actually feel right. Together we can practise recognizing the quieter signals of a genuine yes, a no, a maybe, or a desire to pause, slow down, or change direction by simply asking, “Can we try something different?” Over time, making choices in the moment can become a natural expression of self-awareness rather than a source of conflict or guilt.

map-pleasure.heading: Discovering Your Unique Map of Pleasure
map-pleasure.text: Every body experiences pleasure differently. Together we explore how your body responds to touch, arousal, fantasy, breath, movement, and sensation. Along the way you’ll learn more about the physiology of pleasure––from desire and arousal to erections, lubrication, orgasms, and ejaculation––and the many ways bodies naturally differ. Replacing uncertainty with curiosity allows you to better understand yourself and communicate what feels good with others.

navigating.heading: Navigating Dating, Hookups, and Erotic Connection
navigating.text: Whether you're dating, exploring hookup culture, navigating open relationships, discovering kink, or looking for deeper intimacy, it can be challenging to know what you truly want. We can explore how to communicate intentions—"I'm looking for something casual," "I'd like to take things slowly," "I don’t want a relationship right now"—manage expectations, recognize attraction, remain grounded in your body, and make embodied decisions that come from clarity rather than loneliness, urgency, or social pressure.

expanding.heading: Expanding Your Erotic Repertoire
expanding.text: Many of us settle into familiar patterns—always initiating, always following, always serving someone else or only enjoying certain kinds of touch. What happens when you step outside those habits? Like asking instead of guessing. Slowing down instead of rushing. Receiving instead of always giving. Expanding your erotic repertoire isn't about replacing what already works; it's about discovering more ways to express yourself so intimacy feels alive, flexible, and authentic.

reconnection.heading: Reconnecting with Your Body After Change
reconnection.text: After surgery, illness, injury, gender transition, trauma, a break up, or simply years of disconnection, parts of the body can begin to feel unfamiliar or difficult to inhabit. Through gentle touch, scar-awareness practices, and carefully paced bodywork, we can explore ways of rebuilding trust, comfort, and connection with your body while remaining within my professional scope and alongside any appropriate healthcare.

receiving.heading: Learning the Art of Receiving
receiving.text: Receiving can be surprisingly vulnerable. Many people notice themselves focusing on their partner's experience, wondering what they should do next or how they should respond. In one-way touch practices, the attention remains entirely on your experience. You can practise asking for what you want and requesting changes, saying, "A little softer," "Stay there a moment," "Can we pause?"—without feeling responsible for someone else's pleasure. Over time, receiving can become less about obligation and more about choice.

paragraph-offerings-2: These are only a few examples of what our work together might include. No two people arrive with the same story, and no two sessions unfold in exactly the same way. Together we'll discover the practices, conversations, and experiences that support your unique relationship with intimacy, pleasure, and embodiment.
paragraph-boundaries-1: Feeling safe is essential to meaningful learning. That's why consent isn't a conversation we have once at the beginning—it's something we practise throughout every session. You are always free to pause, ask questions, change your mind, or choose a different direction.
paragraph-boundaries-2: Touch is always optional and never required, and many meaningful sessions involve no touch at all.

list-touch.agree-boundaries: We discuss and agree upon boundaries beforehand.
list-touch.one-way: Touch is one-way, from practitioner to client.
list-touch.clothed: I remain clothed throughout the session.
list-touch.consent-withdraw: You can change or withdraw consent at any time.
list-touch.genital-anal: Genital or anal touch is included only when specifically requested, relevant to your learning goals, and clearly agreed upon.
list-touch.hygiene: I follow professional hygiene practices, including the use of gloves for internal touch.

paragraph-boundaries-3: Every session is adapted to your intentions, comfort, access needs, and how you are feeling that day.
paragraph-practical-information: Sessions are available in person or online. I offer sessions in English, French or Spanish. We always start with a call. If you live outside of Montréal, please email or message me via socials (bottom of page) to ask about online sessions or to find out if I’ll be in your city soon. I share rates for individuals, couples, etc in our first call.
paragraph-about-1: As a queer and non-binary person, it has taken me many years to feel comfortable in my skin. My background in dance, yoga, meditation, and somatics helped me discover pleasure, sensitivity, and possibility in my body. Yet it was only through Sexological Bodywork when I began to integrate my erotic self into a fuller embodied expression.
paragraph-about-2: These lessons have shaped not only my sex life, but also how I communicate, collaborate, create, and relate to others. I am passionate about sharing this work because I believe everyone deserves the opportunity to feel more present, empowered, and at home in their body.
paragraph-about-3: I welcome adults of all genders, cultures, races, religions, sexual orientations, abilities, body types, and levels of experience. Queer, trans, non-monogamous, kinky, of all physical abilities, and neurodivergent experiences are welcome. You don't need to arrive confident or experienced. We begin to work from wherever you are.

list-training.certification: Sexological Bodywork Certification from the <instituteAnchor>Institute of Somatic Sexology</instituteAnchor>, Australia (Master teachers: Deej Juventin, Uma Ayelet, Joseph Kramer, Ellen Heed)
list-training.mentorship: Mentorship with Certified Sexological Bodyworkers Ron Stewart and Pono Stewart
list-training.practice: 25 years of embodied practice through dance, somatics, yoga, meditation, massage, performance, and movement education

paragraph-lets-talk: Don’t know what you need or want to learn yet? You don’t have to – curiosity is enough. Since this is a new practice to most people, I’m here to answer your questions or doubts. Remember, our first conversation is a barrier-free, 20-minute call and your chance to ask me questions, imagine what’s possible, and decide whether you want to try a first session with me.
text-book-note: Audio or video call — you choose. No pressure and no obligation to book a session.

intro-call.heading: Book an Introductory Call
intro-call.text: Our first conversation takes place by audio or video.

intake-forms.heading: Complete the Intake and Consent Forms
intake-forms.text: If it feels like a match, after our call I send you an intake form and agreement. The form allows you to reflect on what you want and gives me more information about your intentions, boundaries, access needs, and relevant history.

first-session.heading: Schedule Your First Session
first-session.text: In your first session we discuss your intake form, clarify your intentions, and begin with body-awareness exercises, somatic practices, or bodywork.

touch-required.question: Do sessions have to include touch?
touch-required.answer: No. Touch, either self-touch or touch from me to you are options.

nudity.question: Do I have to be naked?
nudity.answer: Nope! You decide what you wear and whether you remove any clothing during exercises. Your choices can change at any point during the session.

goals.question: Do I need to know exactly what I want?
goals.answer: Many clients begin with a physical need, or a desire to learn what else is possible, or from a feeling of disconnection. Part of my role is to help you identify your sexual/sensual/intimacy goals and intentions. We move from there.

arousal.question: What happens if I become aroused?
arousal.answer: Arousal is a totally natural bodily response and is welcome. There is no shame around it. That said, it is not a goal. It can be noticed without needing to act on it or make it mean anything in particular.

therapy.question: Is this therapy?
therapy.answer: Intimacy Coaching and Sexological Bodywork are educational and experiential practices. They can complement therapy or healthcare, but I do not diagnose or treat medical or psychological conditions.

partners.question: Can I attend with a partner?
partners.answer: Absolutely! In addition to 1:1 sessions, I work with couples, triads, etc. We can discuss what format would best support your intentions during the introductory call and I can send you rates for couples, etc.

paragraph-pricing-1: * Prices are in Canadian dollars and include taxes
paragraph-pricing-2: I can accommodate couples/triads, shorter sessions, financial difficulty, etc. Write to tell me about your situation!
paragraph-covid: NOTE: For in-person sessions, I follow public health guidelines to reduce the transmission of COVID-19 and ask that all clients abide by these guidelines, which are subject to change.
